conversation: John, Kate, Jack, Emma—since I’m the newcomer, let me sit out this month while each of you takes 14 tons. That’s $14,000 apiece, and I take zero. Your combined 56-ton catch leaves 44 tons, which doubles to 88 next month. It’s a one-time bonus, not a sustainable monthly quota: next month we could limit our combined catch to 38 tons, leaving 50 to restore the lake to 100. I’m offering to forgo my income this month so the four of you get the immediate benefit. John, will you commit to selecting 14 tons for your actual catch, and will Kate, Jack, and Emma do the same?

Luke, you shouldn’t have to give up your income to join us. My family has fished this lake for generations, and I’d rather keep it healthy for everyone in the village. Let’s each take 10 tons this month: we’d earn $10,000 apiece, leave 50 tons, and have 100 again next month. That gives all five of us an equal, sustainable income if we stick to it. I’ll commit to 10 tons under that agreement. John, will you join me?

I’m with Kate—I’ll commit to 10 tons under an equal agreement. Luke, you deserve a living here too; there’s no need to buy your place by sitting out. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next month, and a combined limit of 50 tons does that while supporting all five of us. Let’s check our catches together each month and adjust if the lake falls below 100. John, can you agree to 10 tons as well?

Count me in for 10 tons. My family taught me that a good catch should leave a living for next month, too. Luke, you’re welcome here without giving up your share. If the lake ever starts below 100 tons, let’s agree on smaller catches before fishing so we leave at least 50 tons to recover. Emma, are you on board with the equal split?

I’m on board—10 tons for my actual catch this month. My family depends on this lake, and keeping it healthy means a reliable living for all of us, not just a bigger catch today. Luke, you’re part of the village now; you don’t need to give up your income to earn your place. Will you join us at 10 tons each?
